guides.title: How BeanPool works
guides.summary: Beans, trading, offers and needs, and credit, in plain words.

blocks.text: Beans
Your community trades in **beans**. Beans are not money from a bank. They are a record of who has helped whom.
Everyone starts at zero. When you help someone, you earn beans. When someone helps you, you spend beans.
A rough guide: 40 beans is about one hour of someone's time. You and the other person agree the real price.
Offers and Needs
An **Offer** is something you can do or give: bread, a lift, an hour of gardening, a repair.
A **Need** is something you are looking for.
Before you can post a Need, or ask for someone else's Offer, you must have posted at least one Offer of your own. Everyone brings something.
How a trade works

items: You find an Offer you want and ask for it, or someone takes up your Need.
When the trade is agreed, the buyer's beans are held safely. Nobody can spend them while the trade is going on.
The job gets done.
The buyer confirms it is done. Then the beans go to the seller.

blocks.text: If a trade gets stuck, an admin of your community can step in. They can pay the seller, give the beans back to the buyer, or split them. An admin cannot decide a trade they are part of.
Gifts
You can also send beans to someone as a gift, with no trade.

items: A gift can only come from beans you have. It can never take you below zero.
You can send gifts once you have completed a trade in the market. A trade of only 1 or 2 beans is too small to count.
Gifts have no fee.

blocks.text: Going below zero: your credit line
You can spend a little more than you have, and go below zero. This is your **credit line**. It is a promise to help others later.

Your credit line starts at zero. It opens when you complete your first trade in the market (a trade of only 1 or 2 beans is too small to count). Someone your community has chosen to welcome newcomers can also give you a small start by vouching for you: 25, 50 or 100 beans.
Your credit line grows with your **trust**:

items: You earn trust by completing trades in the market. Gifts do not earn trust.
Trading with many different people builds more trust. Trade with any one person counts up to 500 beans.
Trust grows quickly at first, then more slowly.
Star ratings matter. If people rate you, your average rating scales the trust your trades earn: 5 stars keeps all of it, 1 star keeps 60%.
The deepest any credit line can go is 2,000 beans below zero.

blocks.text: Your Offers unlock your credit
Trust sets how deep you **could** go. Your live Offers set how deep you **may** go right now. You get the smaller of the two.

items: No live Offers: you cannot go below zero.
1 Offer: down to 200 below zero.
2 Offers: down to 500.
3 Offers: down to 1,000.
4 Offers: down to 1,500.
5 Offers: down to 2,000.

blocks.text: If you take Offers down while you are below zero, you may owe more than your Offers now cover. Then you cannot spend more until you are back within your limit. You can still earn beans, and nothing is taken from you.
Trust badges

Your trust shows as a badge. The badges are Newcomer, Resident, Steward and Elder. The trust behind your badge adds up three things: the start a vouch gave you, the trust you earned by trading, and any trust an admin granted you. An admin can give a member a badge directly, without trades.

items: Resident from 200 trust.
Steward from 600 trust.
Elder from 1,400 trust.

blocks.text: A badge is recognition, nothing more. It does not unlock anything. Everyone can trade, invite and vote, whatever their badge.
Fees and the Commons
Your community has a shared pool of beans called the **Commons**. Fees go into it. Members decide together how it is spent.

items: **Market fee:** 1.5% of every market payment goes to the Commons. It comes out of what the seller receives.

**Circulation fee:** beans are meant to move, not sit still. The first 200 beans you hold are always free. Above that, a small monthly fee goes to the Commons: 1% a month on beans between 200 and 500, 1.5% between 500 and 1,000, 2% between 1,000 and 2,000, and 2.5% above 2,000.
Balances below zero never pay the circulation fee. Gifts never pay a fee.

blocks.text: Enterprises and groups

An **enterprise** is a shared project that trades in its own name: a community garden, a bakery, a tool library. It is run by **keepers**, led by a **lead keeper**. Keepers can pledge some of their own trust to give the enterprise a credit line.
A **group** is a circle of members with its own chat and posts, run by one or more **convenors**. One of them is its **lead convenor** — whoever created the group, to begin with.
You can read how keepers and convenors are chosen in "Rules and how decisions work".

guides.title: Rules and how decisions work
guides.summary: Voting, turnout, secret ballots, who may vote, suspension, removing a member, keepers, and convenors and lead convenors.

blocks.text: Two ways to ask the community

items: A **Poll** is a question in the feed, like "Market on Sunday?". It shows what people think. It never changes anything by itself.
A **Decision** is binding. If it passes, your community's server carries it out by itself. Nobody has to press a button, and nobody can quietly ignore it.

blocks.text: What a Decision can do
About a member:

items: Suspend a member, or lift a suspension.
Freeze a member's credit, or unfreeze it.
Give a member the right to vouch for newcomers, or take it away.
Remove a lead keeper from an enterprise.
Remove a member from the community, or reinstate them.

blocks.text: About the Commons:

items: Give beans from the Commons to an enterprise.
Give a hardship grant from the Commons to a member.
Pay off an enterprise's debt from the Commons.

blocks.text: Who can start a Decision

Any active member whose credit is not frozen, and who has traded in the market or was given a trust badge by an admin. A vouch on its own is not enough. Admins can too. You can have one open Decision at a time. You must explain why, in at least 10 characters.
Who can vote
Any active member whose credit is not frozen, and who joined **before** the Decision opened. People who join during a vote cannot vote on it. Enterprise accounts cannot vote.
How votes count

items: Decisions about a member: **one member, one vote**. Yes or No.

Decisions about Commons beans: votes are weighted by trading. You can cast more than one vote, but it gets expensive: 1 vote costs 1 voice credit, 2 votes cost 4, 3 votes cost 9. Your voice credits come from your completed trades, counted up to 500 beans per trading partner. You get your full voice credits again on every Decision. They are never used up.
If you have never completed a trade, you cannot vote on Commons beans yet.
You can change your vote at any time until the vote closes.

blocks.text: Secret ballots

The app never shows anyone how you voted, admins included. Everyone sees the totals, and you see your own vote. Your vote is stored on your community's server with your account, so that it can be counted and checked. The owners and admins who run the server can take a copy of its files, and could look up your vote there.
Polls are different: a Poll is an open show of hands, and everyone can see who picked what.
How long a vote runs
Every Decision runs for exactly 7 days. Voting opens at once. When the 7 days are up, your community's server counts the votes and acts on the result.
Turnout
A vote only counts if enough people take part.

items: Enough people means 30% of the members who could vote and were active in the last 30 days. It is never fewer than 3 people.
For removing a member it is 25%.
"Active" means you did something in the app in those 30 days: posted, traded, voted, sent a message. Only opening the app to look does not count.
Turnout counts people, not the weight of their votes.

blocks.text: If too few people vote, nothing happens. The Decision closes as "unresolved".
How much Yes is needed

items: Most Decisions: 60% Yes.
Removing a member: 66% Yes.
Undoing something (lifting a suspension, unfreezing credit, reinstating a member): more than half.
A tie always fails.

blocks.text: When a Decision passes

items: Your community's server checks that it still makes sense: the member still exists, the Commons has enough beans. Then it acts.
If the Commons is short of beans for a grant, the grant waits until there is enough. It gives up after 90 days.
Only one grant can wait at a time. If a second grant passes while the Commons is still short, it does not wait: it closes for good, and the community must vote again.
If the person or enterprise is already gone, the Decision closes without doing anything.

blocks.text: Removing a member

items: If a removal passes, the member is suspended and their credit frozen at once.
After 7 more days they are removed for good. In those 7 days, a Decision to reinstate them cancels the removal.
When a member is removed, their posts are taken down. If they owed beans, the Commons pays the debt. If they had beans, those beans go to the Commons.
The community can vote to remove anyone except the only owner of your community's server.

blocks.text: Emergency suspension
An admin can suspend a member at once, for example to stop harm. They must give a reason that members can read.

items: At the same moment, a 7-day Decision opens: "Keep this suspension?".
It needs the usual turnout and 60% Yes.
If it does not pass, or too few people vote, the suspension lifts by itself.
An admin cannot suspend themselves, and cannot suspend the server's only owner. Only an owner can suspend another owner.

blocks.text: What admins can and cannot do
Your community's server has owners and admins. They look after it.

items: An admin can stop an open Decision, but must give a written reason. Members can read it on the Decision.
If a removal has passed and is in its 7-day wait, an admin can stop it, or make it happen straight away. If the member being removed is an owner or admin of the server, only an owner can do either.
Admins can give members the right to vouch for newcomers.
Admins can give a member a trust badge. This also gives that member the trust that badge needs, so it deepens their credit line.
Admins sort out stuck trades, but never one they are part of.

blocks.text: Polls

items: Any active member whose credit is not frozen can start a Poll with 2 to 4 answers. It runs for 3, 7 or 14 days.
You can have one open Poll at a time. Your community can have 5 open Polls at once.
A Poll posted to a group can only be answered by that group's members and convenors. Observers can read it but not answer.
Answering a Poll also needs credit that is not frozen. You can change your answer until the Poll closes. The person who started it can close it early.

blocks.text: Enterprises and keepers
An enterprise is run by its keepers. One of them is the lead keeper.

items: **Joining:** you ask to become a keeper and say how much of your earned trust you pledge (it can be 0). You cannot pledge more trust than you have earned by trading, across all your enterprises. The lead keeper approves or declines.
**Objection window:** when an enterprise already has more than one keeper, the lead's approval waits 3 days. Any other keeper can object in that time, and one objection cancels it.
**Removing a keeper:** the lead can remove an ordinary keeper. The same 3-day window applies, and any other keeper can object.

**Community admins:** an admin of your community who is not a keeper of the enterprise can approve a keeper, or remove an ordinary keeper, at once, with no 3-day window. This is so a stuck enterprise can be helped.

**Stepping down:** any keeper can step down. If the enterprise is in debt and your pledge is needed to cover it, you must wait until the debt is smaller or other keepers pledge more. The only keeper cannot step down; they add another keeper first, or wind the enterprise up.
**Your pledge** backs the enterprise's credit line. It is never taken from your own balance or your own credit line.

**A quiet lead:** if the lead keeper has done nothing in the app for 30 days, the other keepers can choose a new lead from among themselves. The vote runs up to 14 days, with Yes and No. It passes when more than half of the other keepers say Yes. If the lead comes back and does anything in the app, the vote is cancelled. Keeper votes cannot be changed.
**If the lead leaves or is removed,** the longest-serving keeper becomes lead at once, and the other keepers can replace them straight away. If no keeper is left, the enterprise is paused.

**Winding up:** the lead keeper, or the only keeper, can start closing an enterprise. So can a community admin. There is then a 7-day wait, and any keeper or a community admin can cancel it. An enterprise in debt cannot close until the debt is paid or the community writes it off. When it closes, any beans left go to the Commons.

blocks.text: Groups and convenors
A group is run by its convenors, and one of them is its **lead convenor**. Whoever creates a group is its first lead convenor.

items: Some groups are open to anyone. Some need a convenor to approve you. Some are by invitation only.

**Any convenor** can approve and invite members, remove a member or an observer, change a member's or an observer's role, make someone a convenor, remove posts and messages, and edit the group and who can join it.
**Only the lead convenor** can remove a convenor, or take the convenor role off someone.
**Nobody can remove the lead convenor, or take the lead off them.** Not another convenor, and not a community admin — admins have no say inside a group.
**Handing the lead over:** the lead can make someone else the lead. It can be another convenor, or a member, who becomes a convenor at the same time. Once it is done, the lead cannot take it back.
**Leaving, as the lead:** hand the lead over first. If nobody else is in the group, the lead can simply leave.
The last convenor cannot step down or be removed while the group still has other members.
Groups do not hold binding votes. To ask a group what it thinks, post a Poll to the group.

**A quiet lead convenor:** if a group's lead convenor has done nothing in the app for 30 days, the group can choose a new one. Its **other convenors** vote — or its **members**, if the lead is the group's only convenor. Any of them can propose someone from that same group of voters, themselves included. The vote runs up to 14 days, Yes or No, in secret. It passes when more than half of those who answer say Yes. If the lead comes back and does anything in the app, the vote is cancelled. The person chosen becomes a convenor and the group's lead. The quiet lead stays a convenor when it was the convenors who voted, and becomes an ordinary member when it was the members. You will find the vote on the group's own screen, above the roster.
**A rogue lead convenor** can be removed by a community Decision. This is coming in a later update.

blocks.text: Vouching

Only members chosen by an admin, or by a community Decision, can vouch for newcomers. A vouch gives the newcomer a small credit line to start with: 25, 50 or 100 beans. Trust badges never give this right.

guides.title: Questions
guides.summary: Short answers to the questions members ask most.

blocks.text: Who runs my community?

Your community runs itself. Its server is looked after by people your community chose: its owners and admins. Your trades, posts and votes are kept on that server. The BeanPool project writes the app, and anyone can use it to start a community.
Is there interest on debt?
No. Being below zero costs nothing. Only beans you hold above 200 pay the small circulation fee.
Can I buy or sell beans for money?
The app has no way to buy or sell beans for money. Beans are earned by helping people.
Why can't I send a gift?
A gift needs two things. You must have completed a trade in the market (1 or 2 beans is too small to count), and you can only give beans you have. A gift can never take you below zero.
Why can't I spend below zero?

Two things set how far below zero you can go. Your trust from trading sets the most you could ever go. Your live Offers set how much of that you may use right now. With no live Offers, you cannot go below zero at all. Most people start by selling: post an Offer, and when someone takes it up, you earn beans and your first trust.
My badge says Steward. Why can I spend so little?
Your badge shows your trust. What you can spend right now also depends on how many live Offers you have. Badges never unlock anything on their own.
Can I change my vote?
On a Decision or a Poll, yes, until the vote closes. On a keeper or convenor vote, no.
Can anyone see how I voted?

On a Decision, the app shows only the totals, and your own vote to you. Your vote is stored on your community's server. The owners and admins who run the server can take a copy of its files, and could look it up there. On a Poll: yes, everyone can see. Polls are an open show of hands.
I lost my phone. Is my account gone?

No, if you kept your 12-word recovery phrase. Install the app and restore your account with those 12 words. If you linked a sign-in account in Account Protection, you can also use that. Keep your 12 words somewhere safe and private. Anyone who has them can use your account.
Can I belong to more than one community?
Yes. You can save several communities in the app and switch between them. You use the same identity in each. Each community has its own beans, rules and members.
I am going away. What should I do?
Turn on Holiday Mode in Settings. Your Offers are hidden and nobody can send you new requests. Finish or cancel any open trades first, because Holiday Mode cannot start while a trade is open.
How do I leave?

You can delete your account in Settings. First finish or cancel any open trades. When you delete your account, any beans you hold go to your community's Commons, and if you are below zero, the Commons covers it. This cannot be undone, even with your 12 words.
Something is wrong or could be better. Who do I tell?
For problems with a person or a trade, talk to the admins of your community. For ideas about the app itself, visit beanpool.org.

guides.title: What's new
guides.summary: What changed in each version of the app, in plain words.

blocks.text: Version 1.2.38
Some of these changes live on your community's server. You get them when your community's server is updated.
New

items: **This BeanPool sheet.** Guides to how BeanPool works, the rules, common questions and what's new. They work without a connection. Open it from Settings → BeanPool.
**Light or dark.** The app starts light. To make it dark, or to have it follow your phone, go to Settings → Appearance: Same as phone, Light or Dark.

**Badges.** Every screen now uses the same trust levels as your community's server: Resident from 200 trust, Steward from 600, Elder from 1,400. Some screens used to show the wrong badge. The Newcomer badge is easier to read.

blocks.text: Voting

items: **Secret ballots.** The app no longer shows anyone how you voted on a Decision, admins included. You can see your own vote.
**Who may vote.** Only members who joined before a Decision opened can vote on it.
**Turnout.** Turnout now counts members who did something in the app in the last 30 days.
**Emergency suspension.** When an admin suspends someone, a 7-day vote opens at once: "Keep this suspension?". If it does not pass, the suspension lifts by itself.
**Voice credits.** The voice credits shown for votes on Commons beans are the ones that count. You get them in full on every such vote.
**Fewer kinds of Decision.** Decisions can no longer change trust badges. The old "voting rounds" are gone.

blocks.text: Enterprises

items: When the lead keeper adds or removes a keeper, the other keepers have 3 days to object.
A keeper can step down, unless they are the only keeper.
Choosing a new lead now has a 14-day limit, and keepers can vote No.
If the lead leaves, the longest-serving keeper takes over at once.

blocks.text: Groups

items: **Every group has a chat.** Talk now has three buttons: **Messages**, **Groups** and **People**. **Groups** lists your groups, the enterprises you keep and the events you are going to, each with its latest message and unread count.

**One way to start a group.** **New group** in Talk and **+** in Commons open the same form, with **Social Circle** chosen for you. After you create it you land in its chat, which asks who you want to invite.
**Invitations.** Convenors can invite people from the chat's menu. An invitation shows who sent it, and **Join the group** takes you straight into the chat.
**Mute a chat** for 8 hours, a week or for good. @mentions still get through.
**One header for every chat**: the group's, enterprise's or event's name at the top. Tap it to see the group, enterprise or event.
The old group chats in Chats have been removed, with their messages.

Every group now has a **lead convenor** — whoever created it, to begin with. Any convenor still looks after members and posts, but only the lead can remove or demote a convenor, and nobody can remove the lead. The lead can hand the lead on to someone else. If the lead goes quiet for 30 days, the group's other convenors — or its members, if the lead is its only convenor — will be able to choose a new one. The screens for that vote come in a later update.

blocks.text: Safety

items: Only an owner can give back or take away an owner's or admin's role.
An admin cannot settle a stuck trade they are part of.
Group and event chats limit how fast one person can post.

blocks.text: Fixes

items: The map has one locate button again.
The Market feed is easier to read in dark mode.

guides.title: Joining BeanPool
guides.summary: Two ways in: a community, with an invite from a member, or the global community, with one sign-in. And how to invite someone else.

blocks.text: Two ways in

items: **With an invite**, you join a community: the people near you, with its own Beans, trades and Commons. A member of that community invites you.

**Without an invite**, you can join the **global community**: people from everywhere, where you can post, message people and find a community near you. There are no Beans there. Beans, credit and the Commons live in local communities.

blocks.text: Either way, your account is a key kept on your phone, with 12 words that bring it back. There is no password.
Joining with an invite
An invite is a link, a QR code or a code. A code looks like **INV-** followed by letters, or a long code that starts with **BP-**.

items: An invite works **once**.
An invite lasts **30 days**. After that, ask for a new one.

blocks.text: To join:

items: Install BeanPool and open it. If you tap an invite link first, the app picks up the invite by itself, even straight after installing it from Google Play.
On the first screen, tap **Join with an invite**. If the invite is on your clipboard, you can tap **Paste** instead. In the web app, the button says **I'm New Here**.
Paste the invite link or code. If you only have a code, also type the community's name or address. The person who invited you can tell you.
Choose the name people will see. It needs at least 2 letters. Keep it short: when you join, names longer than 20 characters are cut short.
Tap **Next**. The app checks the invite and the name. If someone already has that name, it suggests others.

blocks.text: Joining the global community
This is done in the phone app.

items: On the first screen, tap **Explore BeanPool worldwide**.

Sign in once with Google, Apple (on an iPhone), Facebook or GitHub. This keeps out fake accounts: one sign-in account makes one BeanPool account. BeanPool never sees your password and never posts anything for you.
Choose the name people will see, up to 20 characters, and tap **Join**. If someone already has that name, the app suggests others.

blocks.text: The sign-in you used also becomes a way back into your account if you lose your phone, so you are not asked to sign in again at **Safety Backup**. After joining you don't sign in to open the app: your account is the key on your phone, like any other.
The four steps
The bar at the top shows **Your Name**, **Your Photo**, **Safety Backup** and **How it Works**.

items: **Your Photo:** choose a photo or one of the ready-made pictures. You must pick one before **Next** works. People trade more easily with a face or a picture they recognise.

**Safety Backup:** the app shows your 12 words. Write them down on paper and keep them safe. The tickbox **I've saved these words** is there to remind you. Nothing stops you if you skip it, but read "Your 12 words" soon. If you joined the global community, this step also shows your sign-in protecting your account.
**How it Works:** a short tour. Tap **Let's Begin!** to start.

blocks.text: If you close the app halfway, it carries on from the same step next time.
If the invite does not work

items: **Already used:** each invite works exactly once. Ask for a new one. If it was yours and you are already a member, use **Recover an existing account** instead.
**Expired:** invites last 30 days. Ask for a new one.
**Not recognised:** check you copied all of it, and that the community name or address is right.

blocks.text: If joining the global community does not work

items: **Can't reach the global community:** check your connection and tap **Try again**. You can still join a community with an invite.
**This sign-in already has a BeanPool identity:** you joined before, perhaps on another phone. Tap **Restore my account**, then use your 12 words or the same sign-in.
**Too many new accounts from this network:** there is a limit on new accounts from one internet connection. Try again later.
**Not taking new members right now:** join a community with an invite instead.

blocks.text: Inviting someone
Any member can invite people. Your trust badge does not matter.

items: Tap the invite icon (a person with a plus) at the top right of the screen. This opens **Invites**.
If you like, write who the invite is for, just for your own records.
Tap **Generate Ticket**. Without a connection, the button says **Generate Offline Ticket**, and that works too.
Show them the QR code, or tap **Share Invite** to send the link and the code.
Invites nobody has used yet are listed under **Pending**, each with **Share** to send it again.

blocks.text: A community's admins can turn invites off for the whole community.

guides.title: Your 12 words
guides.summary: The 12 words are the key to your account. Why they matter, where to find them, and how to keep them safe.

blocks.text: Why they matter
Your account is not a password kept by someone else. It is a key kept on your phone. Your **12 words** are that key, written as words.

items: With the 12 words, you can get your account back on a new phone: your name, your beans and your trust.
Without them, a lost or broken phone can mean a lost account.

Anyone who has your 12 words can use your account. Never share them, never type them anywhere except the BeanPool app or your own community's BeanPool web app, and never send them in a message. Nobody from BeanPool or your community will ever ask for them.

blocks.text: Write them down

items: Write the 12 words on paper, in order, and check the spelling.
Keep the paper somewhere safe, away from your phone.
A photo or screenshot of the words is easy for someone else to find. Paper is safer.

blocks.text: Where to see them again
Open **Settings** with the sliders button at the top of the screen. Then either:

items: Under **Account & Identity**, tap **View Recovery Phrase**. Type **CONFIRM**, tap **Show Recovery Phrase**, and pass your phone's lock screen check.
Or tap **Account Protection**, then **Show My 12 Recovery Words**. Tap **Hide** when you are done.

blocks.text: A phone restored with a sign-in account gets your 12 words back only if that sign-in account was linked from a phone that had them, on an up-to-date app. Otherwise the phone has no copy of them: they can't be rebuilt from a sign-in. **View Recovery Phrase** is still there, and says **No copy on this phone yet**. On that phone a linked sign-in account is how you get back in, so keep one linked under **Account Protection**.
Put your 12 words back on this phone
If this phone has no copy of your 12 words, and you have them written down, you can add them:

items: Open **Settings**. Under **Account & Identity**, tap **View Recovery Phrase**. (Or, in **Account Protection**, tap **Show My 12 Recovery Words**.) On a phone with no copy, either one opens **Add your 12 words to this phone**.
Type the 12 words in order, or tap **Paste**. Capitals and extra spaces don't matter. A word that is not on the list of recovery words is marked as you type.
Tap **Add these words**.

blocks.text: Your phone checks that the words belong to your account, the same check as **Check your 12 words** for owners. They are not sent anywhere. If they belong to a different account, nothing changes and the app says so. Once they are added, **View Recovery Phrase** shows them, in every community on this phone.
A second way back: a sign-in account

On the phone app you can also link a Google, Facebook or GitHub account (and Apple on an iPhone). If you lose your phone, that account together with your community's server can restore your account on a new phone. See "Getting your account back".

A sign-in account you link from a phone that has your 12 words keeps them too, so restoring with it gives them back. One you linked on an older version of the app brings your account back without them: under **Account Protection**, tap **Connect again** next to it to include them. Keep the paper as well.
In a web browser
The web app has no sign-in recovery. There, your 12 words are the only way back. Browsers can also clear saved data, so write the words down before you rely on the web app.

guides.title: Your profile
guides.summary: Your name, photo, a few words about you, and who can see your contact details.

blocks.text: Change your name, photo or bio

items: Open **Settings** with the sliders button at the top of the screen.
On your card at the top, tap **Edit**, or tap your photo.
Change what you like:
**Callsign** is the name people see.
**Bio** is a few words about you, up to 200 characters.
Tap the photo to change it.
Tap **Save Profile**.

blocks.text: You can also tap **Re-run Setup** in Settings. It walks you through your name and photo again, and the short tour of how BeanPool works.
A name and a photo come first
You need a name and a photo before you can post or accept a trade. If one is missing, the app says **Finish your profile first**. Tap **Set up profile** to add it.
Contact details
Under **Contact details** you can add a phone number, an email or a WhatsApp number. You do not have to.
Once you add one, choose **Who can see this?**:

items: **Hidden:** nobody.
**Trade Partners:** meant for people you trade with. For now it works like Community: every member can see it. To keep it private, choose Hidden or Friends.
**Friends:** people you have added as friends.
**Community:** every member of your community.

blocks.text: Today the web app can show your contact details on your posts. The phone app does not show other members' contact details yet.
What others see
Tap the round picture at the top right of the screen to see your own profile. Other members see much the same:

items: your name, when you joined and your bio;
your trust badge, how many trades you have done, with how many people, and how many you finished;
star ratings and reviews from people you traded with;
your posts.

blocks.text: Your working style

On your profile there is a short, optional quiz, **Take 60s Quiz**. It describes how you like to work with others. On someone else's profile it shows how well your styles fit. It changes nothing else.

guides.title: The top bar
guides.summary: The bean, the small icons that show when something needs you, and the buttons at the top right.

blocks.text: What is in it
The bar at the top of the screen is the same on every tab. From left to right:

items: **The bean:** your community, and this guide.
**The "needs you" icons:** only while something is waiting for you.
**The invite icon, Settings and your picture.**

blocks.text: The bean
Tap the bean at the top left to open the **BeanPool** sheet. It shows:

items: **Your community:** its name, and whether it can be reached right now.
**Your communities:** tap one to switch to it, or tap **Add a community**.
**The guides:** this guide, with its search, and what is new.

blocks.text: The small dot on the bean tells you how things are:

items: **Green:** connected, and you are a member here.
**Amber:** you are visiting as a guest.
**Red:** your community's server cannot be reached right now, or this phone is not connected to a community yet.

blocks.text: A single slow check does not turn the dot red. It only goes red after more than one check fails in a row.
The "needs you" icons
Between the bean and the buttons on the right, small icons appear only while something needs you. Each one is a kind of thing. Tap it to go straight there.

items: **A handshake:** a deal is waiting for you. Someone is waiting for you to accept their request, or a deal you are in is not finished yet. If there is one, the tap opens that deal. If there are more, it opens **My Deals**.
**A ballot box:** a vote you have not cast yet. The tap opens **Commons**, at **Decide**. A vote you cannot cast yet does not count here, for example one that needs you to finish a trade first.

**A speech bubble:** an unread message from a person. If it is from one person, the tap opens that chat. If it is from several people, it opens **Talk**, at **Messages**, showing only the unread ones.
**A group of people:** new lines in your groups or event chats. Chats you have muted stay quiet here. The tap opens the chat, or the unread list in **Messages** if there are several.

**A shield:** only for people who help run your community. It shows while there is admin work waiting, like a report to review or a stalled trade that needs a ruling. The tap asks for your phone's screen lock, then opens your community's settings at that job. If your community's settings use a sign-in code, it asks for that too.

blocks.text: The icons stack from the right. The most important one sits next to the invite icon, and keeps its place as others come and go.
The number and the colour

items: A small number on an icon means more than one of that kind: for example 3 people who wrote to you. It shows **9+** above 9.
An icon turns **amber** when it is more pressing: a deal waiting on you, admin work, or a vote that closes within 2 days. Nothing turns red.

blocks.text: On a small screen
If there is not room for every icon, the last space shows **•••**. Tap it to see the whole list, **Needs you**, in words. Tap a line to go there.
A quiet bar is good news
When nothing needs you, there are no icons at all. You have not missed anything. The icons update as you move around the app and when you come back to it.
Join or Connect
Instead of the icons, you may see a button:

items: **Join** (amber): you are visiting as a guest. Tap it to open **Invites**, where you can join with an invite.
**Connect** (red): this phone is not connected to a community. Tap it to open **Settings**, where you can add one.

blocks.text: While one of these shows, the invite icon is hidden.
The buttons on the right

items: **The invite icon** (a person with a plus): opens **Invites**, to invite someone or join another community. See "Joining BeanPool".
**Settings** (the sliders): opens **Settings**. Tap it again to go back to where you were.
**Your picture:** opens your own profile, as others see it.

blocks.text: Update messages
Sometimes a green bar shows under the top bar:

items: **Update available:** a newer version of the app is out. Tap **Upgrade** to get it, or the cross to close the message.
**Your app is too old for this community:** you need to update before the app works properly here. This one cannot be closed. Tap **Upgrade**.

blocks.text: The tabs
Under the top bar are the tabs: **Market**, **Map**, **Talk**, **Pulse**, **Commons** and **Ledger**. The name of each tab sits above its icon.
On a long page, tap the tab you are already on to jump back to the top. This works on every tab except **Map**.

guides.title: This guide
guides.summary: Where to find this guide, how to search it, and how it stays up to date.

blocks.text: Opening it
Tap the bean at the top left of the screen. Or:

items: Open **Settings** with the sliders button at the top of the screen.
Under **BeanPool**, tap **Help & how it works**.

blocks.text: In the web app, it is in the same place: **Settings**, then **Help & how it works** under **BeanPool**.
What is in it

items: **Your community:** its name, and whether its server can be reached right now. Tap it to switch to another community or add one.
**Guides:** how BeanPool works, the rules and how decisions are made, and common questions.
**How to use the app:** one short page for each task, grouped the way the app is: Market, Map, Talk, Pulse, Commons, Ledger and Settings.
**The BeanPool project:** what is new in this version, and a link to the website beanpool.org, with a **Share** button to send it to a friend.

blocks.text: Searching
Type a word or two in **Search the guide** at the top. It shows every page with all of your words. It works without a connection.

items: Short words work: "vot" finds "vote" and "voting".
If nothing comes up, try one simpler word, like "gift", "photo" or "block".

blocks.text: Always there, kept up to date

The guide is built into the app, so it works with no connection at all. When you are online, the app checks beanpool.org for a newer guide and uses it if there is one. The bottom of the guide shows which version you are reading.
The same guide is on the website at beanpool.org/guide.
Videos

Some pages may show **Watch:** and the name of a video. That link only appears when BeanPool has made a video for that page and your community has it in the Pulse, under **Learn**. Videos members add to Learn never show on a guide page. Every page is complete without the video.

guides.title: Getting help
guides.summary: Where to look when you are stuck, and who to ask.

blocks.text: Look it up

items: **This guide:** search it for a word, like "gift" or "photo".
**The ⓘ buttons:** many screens have a small ⓘ. Tap it for a short explanation of that screen. The Ledger has several.
**The pricing guide:** in **Settings**, under **Community Pricing Guide**, tap **Browse 500+ Item Estimates** to see what things usually cost in beans.

blocks.text: Ask a person

items: **About a trade:** message the other person first. Most problems are misunderstandings. On the post, tap **Message** and their name.
**About a person or a trade that has gone wrong:** talk to the admins of your community. They look after its server, and they can step in on a stuck trade.
**About the app itself:** visit beanpool.org. You can open it from **Settings**, under **BeanPool**.
**Running a community yourself:** the owners and admins who run a community's server have their own manual, in that server's Settings: sign in and press **Manual** in the side bar.

**Getting into Settings:** owners and admins see **Community admin** in the phone app's **Settings**. **Manage** opens Settings on the phone. On a computer, open Settings in a web browser and choose **Sign in with your phone**, then in the app tap **Sign in on a computer** and scan the code. Check the 6-character code on the phone matches the one on the computer before you tap **Sign in**.

blocks.text: When something is not right

items: If a post is a scam, offensive or misleading, report it. See "Reporting a problem".
If someone is bothering you, block them. See "Blocking someone".

blocks.text: Safety pages
In **Settings**, under **Legal & Privacy**, you can read the **Privacy Policy**, the **Terms of Service & EULA** and the **Child Safety Standards**. They open on beanpool.org.

guides.title: More than one community
guides.summary: Belong to several communities with one account, and switch between them.

blocks.text: One account, several communities
Your phone holds one account: one name, one key, one set of 12 words. You can use it to join more than one community. Each community keeps its own beans, trades and posts.
Joining another community

items: A community needs an invite from one of its members.
Tap the invite icon (a person with a plus) at the top right of the screen to open **Invites**.
Under **Join Another Community**, paste the invite link or code. If you only have a code, also fill in the community's address.
Tap **Join Community**.

blocks.text: The global community needs no invite, but for now it is joined from the app's first screen, before you have an account: tap **Explore BeanPool worldwide** there. See "Joining BeanPool". Joining it from an account you already have is not possible yet.
Switching

items: Tap the bean at the top left. The **BeanPool** sheet opens, with **Your communities** near the top.
Tap the one you want.

blocks.text: You can also switch in **Settings**, under **System**, then **Advanced / Subsystem**. Your communities are listed there. The one you are using is marked as active. Tap **Switch to Town** on another one to move to it.
Forgetting a community on this phone

items: In **Advanced / Subsystem**, tap **Forget** on a community you are not using right now. This removes it and its saved data from this phone.
In the **BeanPool** sheet, under **Your communities**, pressing and holding a community and tapping **Remove** only takes it off the list. Its data stays on the phone.

blocks.text: Neither deletes your account there, and your other communities are not affected.
Visiting as a guest
If you add a community without an invite, you are a guest there. A **Join** button shows at the top, next to the bean. A guest sees very little until they register with an invite.

guides.title: Using BeanPool in a web browser
guides.summary: The web app does most of what the phone app does. Where its buttons have different names.

blocks.text: The same account, a different screen
Your community can also be used in a web browser, on a computer or a phone. This guide is written for the phone app. The web app works the same way, but some things are named or placed differently.
Different names and places

items: **Tabs:** the web app has **Market**, **Pulse**, **Map**, **Commons**, **Chat**, **People** and **Ledger**. What the phone app calls **Talk** is **Chat** on the web, and **People** has its own tab.
**Settings and your profile:** the two small buttons at the top right. On a wide screen they are at the bottom of the menu on the left.
**Posting an Offer or a Need:** use **New Post** on the **Map** page.
**Appearance:** the choice is called **Same as device** instead of "Same as phone".
**Blocking:** Settings says **Manage Blocked Members**.
**Chats:** the web chat has **Report** and **Block** buttons at the top.

blocks.text: What the web app does not have

items: Signing in with Google, Facebook, GitHub or Apple to get your account back. On the web, your 12 words are the only way back.
The Pulse's **Learn** lane.
The phone's app lock.

Signing in to your community's Settings with your own key, for owners and admins. The web app's **Manage** link opens Settings, but a browser has no unlock of its own. On the computer, choose **Sign in with your phone** in Settings and scan the code with the phone app (**Settings**, then **Sign in on a computer**).

blocks.text: Using your phone account on a computer

items: In the web app on the computer, choose to link with the mobile app. It shows a QR code.
On the phone, open **Settings** and tap **Link Another Device**.
Point the phone's camera at the QR code and tap **Confirm & Link Device**.

blocks.text: Installing it
The web app may offer **Install BeanPool** so it opens from your home screen like an app. If your browser cannot do that, tap **How?** for steps.
Keep your 12 words

Browsers sometimes clear saved data, for example Safari after a week without a visit. Until you have looked at your 12 words, the web app's Settings shows a warning with **View & Save Recovery Phrase**. Do it, and write them down.

guides.title: Browsing the market
guides.summary: Find Offers and Needs with search, filters and distance.

blocks.text: The Market tab
Tap **Market** in the row of tabs. You see what people in your community are offering and looking for, newest first, grouped by the day they were posted. Events come first.
Pull the list down to refresh it.
The search and filters slide away as you scroll down, so you see more posts. Scroll up a little and they come back. To jump back to the top, tap **Market** again.
Search

Type in **Search marketplace...** at the top. On a small phone it may just say **Search**. The search also finds related words: "fruit" finds "lemon". Without a connection, it searches what is already on your phone.
Filters
The row of buttons under the search chooses what you see:

items: **All**, **Offers** or **Needs**.
**For You:** only the categories you star under **Customize interests**.
**Events** and **Polls**.

blocks.text: The second row narrows it down:

items: **All Categories:** pick one category, like Food, Tools or Garden.
**Distance:** only posts within a distance of a point. See "Finding things near you".
**Trust:** only posts by members who have not traded yet (**Founding**), by **Newcomers**, or by members with at least a certain trust badge.
**Beans only:** hides posts that also ask for some cash.

blocks.text: If you belong to groups, a row of group buttons appears too. **All Groups & Public** shows everything; a group's button shows only posts for that group.
If nothing matches, tap **Clear All Filters**.
When you have scrolled down and a search or filter is on, a small chip at the top shows what it is. Tap the chip to change it. Tap **✕** on it to clear the search and every filter.
The button next to **My Deals** changes how the list looks: a list, a grid, or compact.
What a post shows

items: a photo, or the category's picture;
**OFFER** or **NEED**;
the price in beans, with **/Hr** if it is priced by the hour;
**RECURRING** if it stays open after each deal;
**CASH TOO** if the person also needs some cash, for fuel or materials;
a lock and a group name if only that group can see it;
who posted it, with their trust badge and stars. A member who has not traded yet shows **FOUNDING**.

blocks.text: Tap a post to open it.
On a post

items: **Message** and their name: ask a question before you commit.
Tap their name to see their profile, reviews and trust.
**Report Post** if it is a scam, offensive or misleading.
**Block User** to hide their posts and chats on your phone. It also tells your admins. See "Blocking someone".

blocks.text: You cannot save or share a post yet.

guides.title: Posting an Offer or a Need
guides.summary: Put up something you can do or give, or something you are looking for.

blocks.text: Offer first

You must have posted at least one **Offer** before you can post a **Need** or take up someone's Offer. Everyone brings something. How many Offers you have up also decides how far below zero you can go. See "Your credit line".
Before you start
You need a name and a profile photo. If one is missing, the app asks you to **Set up profile** first.
Posting

items: Tap **+ ADD POST** on the Market tab or the Map.
Choose **Offer** or **Need**. The form opens on the Map.
**Title:** a few words, up to 50 characters. "Sourdough loaf", "Lift to town on Fridays".
**Category:** pick the closest one.
**Description:** what, when, where, anything people should know.
**Photos:** at least one, up to five. Tap **Camera** or **Gallery**.

**Location:** tap **My location**, or **Drop a pin** and tap the map, then **Confirm Pin**. Anyone who opens your community's map can see the pin, including people who have not joined, so drop it near you rather than on your front door if you prefer. See "Where your pin goes".

**Price:** a number of beans. Tap the unit button to choose **Total** or **/ Hr**. Tap **FREE** to give it away. The button also offers **/ Dy**, **/ Wk** and **/ Mo**, but a new post does not keep them yet: it is saved as a total price. Choose **Total** and say the period in the description.
Tap **Post Offer** or **Post Need**.

blocks.text: Until everything needed is filled in, the button tells you what is missing, like **Add a photo** or **Set a price**.
Not sure what to charge?

Tap **Not sure what to charge?** under the price. A rough guide: 40 beans is about an hour of someone's time. The **Community Pricing Guide** has estimates for many everyday things. Tapping one fills in an Offer for you.
Below the price you see what you will receive after the 1.5% market fee. Gifts have no fee.
Extra choices

items: **Repeatable:** the post stays up after each deal, and several people can take it at once. Good for a weekly lift or bread every Saturday.
**Cash also needed:** tick this if you also need some cash, for fuel or materials. The app never handles cash; you sort that out between you.
**Where does this travel?** Only if your community trades with other communities: keep the post here, or share it further.

blocks.text: The app keeps a draft as you type. If you leave and come back, it asks whether to **Continue** or **Start fresh**.
Posting only to a group
Open **Commons**, then **Groups**, then your group, and tap **Post to** and the group's name. Only that group sees it. This shorter form has no photos and no location.
Changing or removing a post
Open your post. If no deal is under way on it:

items: **Edit Post** changes the words, category, price and photos. Tap **Save**. The location cannot be changed; delete the post and post it again instead.
**Pause Offer** hides an Offer for a while. **Activate Offer** brings it back. Needs cannot be paused.
**Delete Post** removes it. Anyone still asking for it sees their request marked declined.

blocks.text: Posts do not expire. Delete them when they are done.

guides.title: My Deals
guides.summary: One place for every trade you are in, every post you have up, and your past trades.

blocks.text: Opening it
Tap **My Deals** at the top of the Market tab. A red number on it counts your deals in progress.
Three tabs

items: **In Progress:** deals under way, and requests waiting for an answer. Each shows where it stands: **Held in Trust** (the beans are held), **Action Required** (someone has asked and you need to answer) or **Awaiting Approval** (you asked and are waiting for them).
**My Posts:** your Offers and Needs that are up, or **PAUSED**. A post someone has asked for shows **Action Required**.
**History:** finished, cancelled and declined deals. Choose **All**, **Received** or **Given**. Each shows the date, the amount and the other person.

blocks.text: Tap a deal in **In Progress** or **My Posts** to open the post. That is where you accept, finish or cancel a deal. A request nobody answers ends by itself after 7 days.
Reviews
A finished trade in **History** has a **Review** button. After you review, it says **Edit**, and you can change your stars.

guides.title: A deal, step by step
guides.summary: From asking to getting paid, for an Offer and for a Need, and leaving a review.

blocks.text: The idea

When a deal starts, the person paying has their beans **held in trust**. Nobody can spend held beans. When the job is done, the person paying releases them and the other person is paid. The screens call the beans "credits" in a few places; they mean the same thing.
Taking up someone's Offer

items: Open the Offer and tap **Accept Offer**.
If it is priced by the hour, say how many hours.
Tap **Confirm**. Your beans are held straight away, and the seller is told. There is no waiting for the seller to say yes.
A chat with the seller opens. Agree when and where.

blocks.text: You need to have posted an Offer of your own first. If you have not, the app offers **Create an Offer**.
Helping with someone's Need

items: Open the Need and tap **Offer to Fulfill**, then **Confirm**.
The person who posted it decides. Until then you can tap **Withdraw Request**. If they do not answer in 7 days, the request ends by itself and you are both told.
They see your request under **Fulfillment Requests**, and can **Message** you, **Deny** it or **Approve & Commit**.
When they approve, their beans are held. Unless the post is Repeatable, anyone else who offered sees their request marked declined.

blocks.text: While the beans are held
Both of you see a **Message** button to talk, and **Cancel Trust Hold** to call it off.

items: Do the job, or hand over the thing.

The person paying taps **Release Credits**, then **Release Credits** again to confirm. For hourly work they first enter the hours actually worked. If it was less, the rest goes back to them. If it was more, the extra is taken from them.
The seller is paid at once, less the 1.5% market fee, which goes to your community's Commons.

blocks.text: Only the person paying can release the beans. There is no time limit: beans stay held until they are released or the deal is cancelled. After a week, and every week after that, the person paying gets a reminder.
A Repeatable post
A Repeatable post goes back up after each deal, and several people can be in a deal on it at once. Any other post is marked finished.
Reviews
After releasing, the person paying is asked to rate the deal: 1 to 5 stars and a short, optional comment. Tap **Submit Rating**, or **Skip for now**.

Both people can rate later: tap **Rate** and the name on the finished post (not on a Repeatable post, which goes back up), or **Review** in My Deals, History. You can change your rating; the new one replaces the old.
Stars matter. A low average reduces how much trust the other person earns from their trades. Be fair.

guides.title: When a deal goes wrong
guides.summary: Cancelling a deal, and what happens when you cannot agree.

blocks.text: Talk first
Most problems are a misunderstanding. Tap **Message** on the post and talk it through.
Cancelling

items: **Before it is agreed:** the person who asked taps **Withdraw Request**. The person who posted a Need taps **Deny**, then **Decline**, and can add a short message. A request nobody answers ends by itself after 7 days.

**While the beans are held:** either of you can tap **Cancel Trust Hold**, then **Yes, Cancel**. All the held beans go back to the person paying, and the post goes back on the market. The other person is told.

blocks.text: Either person can cancel alone, at any time before the beans are released. That includes after the work is done. If that happens to you, talk to them, and then to your community's admins.
When you cannot agree
There is no "dispute" button in the app. Ask the admins of your community for help. They look after its server, and they can settle a stuck deal in one of three ways:

items: pay the seller (the normal 1.5% fee applies);
give all the beans back to the buyer;
split them half and half.

blocks.text: An admin cannot settle a deal they are part of, or one involving an enterprise they keep.
You both get an alert and a line in your chat saying how it was settled. It names the admin by their callsign, or says "a community admin".
If someone is not honest

items: Leave a fair review. Low stars reduce the trust they earn.
Report their post, or block them. See "Reporting a problem" and "Blocking someone".

guides.title: What the map shows
guides.summary: The pins on the Map, what their colours mean, and the buttons around them.

blocks.text: Pins
Tap **Map** in the row of tabs. The map shows your community's posts:

items: **Green pins:** Offers.
**Orange pins:** Needs.
**Purple pins with a calendar:** events that have not finished yet.

blocks.text: A pin shows the post's category picture. Where many Offers and Needs are close together, they join into a blue circle with a number. Zoom in to see them one by one. Events always show on their own.
People, groups and enterprises are not on the map. Neither are polls.
Tapping a pin

items: **An Offer or a Need:** a card shows the title and who posted it. Tap **View Details** to open it, or their name to see their profile. Tap the map or **✕** to close the card.
**An event:** a card shows when and where, and how many are going. Tap **View event**.

blocks.text: Filters
At the top of the map:

items: **All**, **Offers**, **Needs** or **Events**. Tap **✕** to clear.
**All Categories** to show one category.
For events: **Today**, **This weekend** or **Next 7 days**. The map moves to fit them.

blocks.text: Buttons on the left

items: The moon or sun: a dark or light map.
The target: show where you are. The first time, the app asks for permission to use your location.

blocks.text: The amber circle shows the area your community serves.
Adding a post from the map
Tap **+ ADD POST**. See "Posting an Offer or a Need".

guides.title: Where your pin goes
guides.summary: Who sees where your posts and events are, and how to keep your home private.

blocks.text: You choose the spot
Every Offer and Need has a place on the map. You choose it when you post:

items: **My location** uses where your phone is right now.
**Drop a pin** lets you tap any spot on the map.

blocks.text: Anyone who opens your community's map can see the pin at that spot, to within about 10 metres. That includes people who have not joined. The app does not blur it for you.

**If you post from home and do not want people to know your address, use Drop a pin and put it somewhere nearby instead:** a corner, a park, the shops. You can tell the other person the exact place in a message once you have agreed.
You cannot move the pin later. To change it, delete the post and post it again.
Events
When you create an event, place the pin first, then tap **Approximate (~100 m)**. The pin then shows only roughly where it is. If you move the pin afterwards, tap it again.

Everyone can see the event's place name, so do not type your home address there. Put the exact address in **Note for people who are going**, which only the hosts and the people who tap **Going** can read.
What is never shown

items: Your own position. The blue dot that shows where you are is only on your phone.
Polls have no place on the map.

guides.title: Finding things near you
guides.summary: Show only posts within a distance of you, or of any place you choose.

blocks.text: On the Market tab

items: Tap **Market**, then **Distance** in the second row of filters. It is not there while **Events** is chosen.
**Location & Radius** opens. To use where you are, tap the target button. Or tap the map, or drag the pin, to choose another centre.
Choose how far with **Search radius**: from 100 metres to 50 kilometres.
Tap **Apply**. The button then shows the distance, like **5km**.
To go back to everything, open it again and tap **Reset**.

blocks.text: Posts with no location are always shown.
The picker opens on a fixed spot, not on you. Tap the target button, or tap the map, before you tap **Apply**.
On the Map
The map has no distance filter. Tap the target button on the left to see where you are, then look around and zoom.
Events near you
Event cards show how far away they are once you have let the app use your location.

guides.title: Messages
guides.summary: Start a chat, send photos, reply, react, edit, delete, mute, and what is private.

blocks.text: Your chats
**Talk** has three buttons at the top: **Messages**, **Groups** and **People**.
Tap **Talk** in the row of tabs, then **Messages**. Your chats with people are listed under **Inbox**. Deals that need you are at the top, under **Action Required**.
Chats that belong to a group, an enterprise or an event are under **Groups**, not here. See "Groups".

items: Search with **Search chats, posts, partners...**.
The filter button sorts by **Recent**, **Unread** or credits, and can show **Unread Only** or **Friends Only**.
The search and filter button slide away as you scroll down. Scroll up a little and they come back. Tap **Talk** again to jump to the top.

blocks.text: Starting a chat

items: From a post: tap **Message** and the person's name.
From **Talk**: tap the pencil button, then find the person by name.
From your friends: **Talk**, then **People**, then **Friends**, and tap the message button next to a name.

blocks.text: Sending

items: Type in **Message...** and tap the send button.

To send a photo, tap **+**, then **Camera** or **Gallery**. In the web app, use the **📎** button, or paste or drag a picture straight into the chat — it shows you the picture first, and anything you have already typed goes with it as a caption. Photos can only be sent in chats between two people.

blocks.text: The ticks under your message:

items: one tick: sent;
two blue ticks: read;
a clock: still sending;
**not delivered**: it failed. Tap it to **Resend** or **Discard** it.

blocks.text: Reply, react, edit, delete
Tap a message. Small round buttons appear beside it:

items: **Reply** quotes it above what you write next. Tap the quote in a sent message to jump back to what it answers.
**React** opens seven emojis. Tap one to add it, tap it again to take it back. One reaction each; tapping a different one swaps it. The reactions show as a small badge under the message.
**Edit**, on your own messages, for 15 minutes after you sent it. The message then shows **edited**. Photos cannot be edited.

**Delete**, on your own messages, at any time — there is no time limit. It asks **Delete for everyone?** once. The message then reads **This message was deleted** for both of you, and nobody can react to it or reply to it.

blocks.text: The same buttons are in a group's chat. See "Groups".
Deleting takes the words off your community's server too, so a new phone signing in later never sees them.
Muting a chat
Tap **⋮** at the top right, then **Mute notifications**: **For 8 hours**, **For a week** or **Always**. Tap **⋮** and **Unmute** to undo it. See "Muting a chat".
What is private

items: A chat between two people is **end-to-end encrypted**: it is locked on your phone and unlocked on theirs, so your community's server cannot read it. One exception: if the app cannot find the other person's key, or locking fails, it sends the message without the lock rather than not at all, and does not warn you. The chat shows **End-to-end encrypted** at the top. Photos in it are encrypted too.
Group, enterprise and event chats are not encrypted. The people who run your community's server can read all of them.
Deleting a message asks your community's server to replace it. It cannot reach a copy someone has already read, or a screenshot.
A group's chat can also be read by the group's members.
An event's chat can also be read by the host and everyone going.

An enterprise's chat can be read by any member of your community. It is the enterprise's public discussion, the same one its page shows, and anyone in the community can write in it too. It is not a private chat for its keepers.

blocks.text: Blocking someone from a chat
Tap their name at the top of the chat. Their profile opens. Tap **Block**, then **Block User**. See "Blocking someone".

guides.title: Groups
guides.summary: Your groups and their chats, talking in them, starting a group, inviting people, and joining by invitation.

blocks.text: What a group is

A group is a place for some people rather than everyone: your street, a garden crew, a choir, a guild. Every group has its own chat. Groups do not hold beans. Being in one does not change your trust or your vote.
Your groups

Tap **Talk**, then **Groups**. Every group you are in is listed there, newest message first, with the enterprises you keep (🥖) and the events you are going to (📅). An enterprise's chat is its public discussion: any member of your community can read it. See "Messages". Each shows its latest message and how many you have not read.

items: The number on **Groups** at the top adds up your unread messages, except in chats you have muted.
Tap a group to open its chat. That marks it read.
Pull the list down to refresh it.

blocks.text: The same list is in **Commons**, under **Groups**, as **Your groups**, without the unread numbers. It opens the same chats.
Starting a group

items: In **Talk**, under **Groups**, tap **New group**. Or in **Commons**, under **Groups**, tap the round **+** button. Both open the same **Create a Group** form.
Give it a **Group Name** and, if you like, a **Purpose / Description**.
Choose a **Category**: **Social Circle** is chosen for you; the others are **General**, **Working Group**, **Project Team** and **Guild**.
Choose a **Join Policy**: **Open**, **Request to Join** or **Invite Only**.
Tap **Create Group**. You become its **lead convenor**, and the app takes you straight into the new group's chat.

blocks.text: Running something together, with beans involved? Tap **Start an enterprise** at the bottom of the categories instead. See "Enterprises".
Inviting people
A new group's chat asks **Who do you want to invite?**

items: Tap **Invite people**, tick the people you want, and tap the button at the bottom (for example **Invite 2 people**).
Or tap **Not now** to skip it.

blocks.text: Later, a convenor can invite people from the chat's **⋮** menu, **Invite people**. Each person you invite sees the group in **Commons**, under **Groups**, marked **INVITED**. When they join, the chat says so.
The group's chat

items: Tap the group's name at the top of the chat to see the group: its members, **Leave Group**, and for convenors, **Convenor Tools**.
The **⋮** menu has **Invite people** (convenors), **Mute notifications** and **Group info**.
Joins, leaves and role changes show in the chat as small grey lines.
Write **@** and someone's name to alert them. See "Mentions".
The newest message sits just above the message box, and stays there when the keyboard opens. Scroll up to read back; a new message arriving then waits for you rather than dragging you down.

blocks.text: A group's chat is not end-to-end encrypted. Its members and the people who run your community's server can read it. The chat says so above the message box. Private things belong in a chat between two people.
Talking in a group's chat
A group's chat works exactly like a chat with one person. Tap a message and small round buttons appear beside it:

items: **Reply** quotes it above what you write next. Tap the quote to jump back to what it answers.
**React** opens seven emojis. One each; tap it again to take it back. The reactions show as a badge under the message.
**Edit**, on your own messages, for 15 minutes. The message then shows **edited**.
**Delete**, on your own messages, at any time. It asks **Delete for everyone?** once, and the message then reads **This message was deleted** to everyone in the group.
**Remove**, for convenors, on anybody else's message. It asks once, and the message then reads **Removed by a convenor**. Your own message is a **Delete**, not a **Remove**.

blocks.text: Under your own message: a clock while it is sending, a tick once the group's server has it, or **! not delivered** if it could not be sent — tap that to **Resend** or **Discard** it. There are no blue double ticks in a group: a group has no single reader.
Photos cannot be sent in a group's chat, and a deal cannot be started in one. Both belong in a chat between two people. See "Messages".
An **observer** can read the chat but not write in it, react or reply.

Your community's server needs to be up to date for reply, reactions, edit and delete. Only if yours is not does the app say **Not available on this community yet** — that one is worth taking to whoever looks after the server.

Anything else the server turns down, it turns down in its own words, and the app shows you those words rather than that line. "A removed message cannot be edited" means a convenor removed it while you were typing, not that your server is behind.
Joining a group
In **Commons**, under **Groups**, **Groups you could join** lists the groups you are not in. Filter them by kind with the buttons above the list. Open a group, then:

items: **Join Group** if it is open to anyone;
**Request to Join** if a convenor approves members. You see **Request Pending Approval** until they do.

blocks.text: An **Invite Only** group is hidden from everyone who is not in it or invited to it.
If a convenor removed you from a group, you cannot join it again by yourself.
Joining by invitation

A group you are invited to shows in **Commons**, under **Groups**, marked **INVITED**. Tap it to see the invitation: who invited you, what the group is, who is in it, and that its chat is not private.

items: Tap **Join the group**. You land in its chat.
Tap **Not now** to decide later. The invitation stays.
If it says **This invitation is no longer open**, it was withdrawn. Ask whoever invited you to invite you again.
If it says **Couldn't open this group**, your phone could not reach your community's server. Tap **Try again**.

blocks.text: Posting to a group
Tap the group's name at the top of its chat, then **Post to** and its name. Only the group's members see the post. It shows in the Market with a lock and the group's name.
Convenors and the lead convenor
A convenor looks after the group. Whoever created it is its **lead convenor**, and the group's card names them, as **Lead convenor: Ali**. In the members list their row is marked **LEAD**.
Under **Convenor Tools**, any convenor can:

items: change the join policy;
**Approve** or **Decline** requests to join;
change a member's or an observer's role — including making them a convenor;
remove a member or an observer;
remove a post or a message;
edit the group.

blocks.text: Only the **lead convenor** can remove a convenor, or take the convenor role off someone. Beside a row you cannot act on, no **Role** or **✕** is shown at all — that is the app telling you it is not yours to do.
**Nobody can remove the lead convenor, or take the lead off them.** Not another convenor, and not a community admin.

**Handing the lead over.** The lead can pass it on: **Hand over** in **Convenor Tools**, or the shield button beside someone's name. Choose another convenor, or a member — a member becomes a convenor at the same time. An observer cannot be the lead; make them a member or a convenor first. Once it is done, you cannot take the lead back.
**Leaving as the lead.** Hand the lead over first; the app offers you that when you tap **Leave Group**. If nobody else is in the group, you can simply leave.
The last convenor cannot step down or leave while anyone else is still in the group.

**When the lead goes quiet.** Nobody can take the lead off the lead, so a lead who stops using the app would leave the group stuck. After 30 days with no activity from them, the group can vote a new lead in instead. Open the group and look just above the **Roster**: a panel appears there naming the lead and how long they have been away. Nothing shows while a group's lead is active — apart from one line saying how the last vote ended, which stays for two weeks after it closes.

Who votes is the group's **other convenors** — or its **members**, if the lead is its only convenor. Any of them can tap **Propose** beside a name in that panel, including their own; proposing counts as that person's Yes. Everyone who can vote then sees **Yes** and **No**. You are asked to confirm, because a vote cannot be changed, and you only ever see the totals — never who voted which way. The vote runs for 14 days and passes when more than half of those who answer say Yes. If the quiet lead comes back and does anything in the app, the vote closes at once. Observers can see the panel but have no vote, and neither does the quiet lead.
The full rules are in "Rules and how decisions work", under "A quiet lead convenor".
Coming soon

items: Removing a rogue lead convenor by a community Decision. Coming in a later update.
Groups in the web app. Today the new Groups list, chats and invitations are in the phone app.

guides.title: People and friends
guides.summary: Find members of your community, add friends, and vouch for someone.

blocks.text: Finding people
Tap **Talk**, then **People**. There are three buttons:

items: **Friends:** people you have added.
**Community:** every member. Search by name, and sort by **Newest**, **Name**, **Friends**, **Trusted** or **Active**.
**Invites:** invite someone new. See "Joining BeanPool". If you have not joined yet, this button says **Register**.

blocks.text: Tap a person to see their profile: their trust badge, trades, reviews and posts.
Friends

items: In **Community**, tap **+ Add** next to a name. It changes to **Added**. Tap **Added** to take them off again.
In **Friends**, tap the message button to start a chat, or the remove button, then **Remove**, to take someone off.

blocks.text: Friends are a shortcut for you. If you choose **Friends** for your contact details, only they can see them. See "Your profile".
Vouching for someone

Some members are chosen by the community to welcome newcomers. They can vouch for a new member, which gives that person a small credit line to start with. On the person's profile, they tap **Vouch for Member** and choose **Light** (25), **Standard** (50) or **Deep** (100). No beans leave the voucher's own wallet.
Who may vouch is decided by an admin or by a community Decision, never by a badge. See "Rules and how decisions work".

guides.title: Event chat
guides.summary: Talk with the host and everyone going to an event.

blocks.text: Who is in it

Every event has its own chat. The host and everyone who has tapped **Going** can read it and write in it. If you change to **Interested**, or tap **Going** again to clear it, you leave the chat. The host is always in it.
Opening it

items: Open the event and tap **Open event chat**.
Or find it in **Talk**, under **Groups**, marked 📅 **Event**.

blocks.text: At the top, a pinned box shows the host's **Note for people who are going**, such as the exact address. Tap the event's name at the very top to go back to the event.
Writing
Type in **Message everyone going…** and tap the send button. You can send up to 30 messages a minute. The newest message sits just above the message box and stays there when the keyboard opens.
Good to know

items: Event chats are not end-to-end encrypted. The host, everyone going, and the people who run your community's server can read them. The chat says so above the message box.
The host can remove any message. Tap it, then **Remove**. It then says "removed by the host".
An event chat has no reply, no reactions, no editing and no deleting your own message — unlike a chat with a person or a group's chat. Ask the host to remove something you regret.
When the event ends or is cancelled, the chat becomes read-only. Some time later it goes away.

guides.title: Muting a chat
guides.summary: Silence a chat — one person's, a group's or an enterprise's — for 8 hours, a week, or for good.

blocks.text: Muting a chat
In any chat with a person, a group or an enterprise:

items: Tap **⋮** at the top right, then **Mute notifications**.
Choose **For 8 hours**, **For a week** or **Always**.

blocks.text: To undo it, tap **⋮**, then **Unmute**.
What muting does

items: It stops that chat's alerts. In a group's chat, someone who @mentions you still reaches you. See "Mentions".
An enterprise's chat sends no alerts, so there are none to stop. Muting it keeps it out of the numbers below.
The chat still shows new messages.
In **Talk**, under **Groups**, a muted chat shows a bell with a line through it. Its unread number is grey, and it is not added to the number on **Groups**.
The top bar stays quiet about it too.
The mute stays when you leave the chat. When you open a group's or an enterprise's chat again, the top says **muted**.

blocks.text: Other chats
Event chats cannot be muted yet. You can:

items: turn off whole kinds of alerts in **Settings**, under **Notification Preferences**. See "Notifications";
block someone who is bothering you. See "Blocking someone".

guides.title: Mentions (@name)
guides.summary: Alert someone in a group chat by writing @ and their name.

blocks.text: Mentioning someone

In a group's chat, write **@** followed by the person's name as it shows in the app, for example "@Ana, can you bring gloves?". They get an alert that you mentioned them, even if they have muted the chat.

items: Capital letters do not matter.
The name must be written in full, and not run on into other letters: "@Anabel" does not alert Ana.
Only people in the group can be mentioned.

blocks.text: Where mentions work
Only in group chats. Posts, event chats and chats between two people do not use them.

guides.title: The Pulse
guides.summary: What your neighbours make and share elsewhere, in one feed.

blocks.text: What it is
Tap **Pulse** in the row of tabs. The Pulse gathers what members of your community post on other sites: videos, music, blogs, photos. It is a way to find out what your neighbours make and do.

items: **Neighbours:** posts from members' channels. The buttons along the top pick a subject, like Food & growing or Repair & reuse. **All** shows everything.
**Learn:** videos about how BeanPool works, and a short daily reflection. See "The Learn lane".

blocks.text: Pull down to refresh.
The buttons along the top slide away as you scroll down. Scroll up a little and they come back. Tap **Pulse** again to jump to the top.
Opening a post

**A YouTube video:** tap the picture, with the ▶ on it, and the video plays here in the card. Nothing is loaded from YouTube until you tap — scrolling past a video sends nothing to anyone. Tap the button in the corner of the video to fill the screen.
The video stops when you scroll it out of sight, when you leave the Pulse, and when you start a different one. Only one plays at a time.
**Everything else** — TikTok, Instagram, a blog, a website: tap the picture or the title and it opens in your browser or in that site's own app.

You can always open a video on YouTube instead: tap the title, or **Open on YouTube ↗** underneath it. If a video will not play here — some people do not allow their videos to play outside YouTube, and some phones cannot — the card says so and offers you that button.
Something wrong with a post

items: **Someone else's post:** tap the flag, choose why (**Spam or scam**, **Offensive content**, **Misleading post** or **Other**) and tap **Submit report**. The people who run your community's server look at it.
**Your own post:** tap **Hide**, then **Hide from feed**. It comes off the Pulse for everyone.

blocks.text: You cannot hide someone else's post just for yourself.
Adding your own
Tap **+ Channels** at the top. See "Sharing your channels".

guides.title: The Learn lane
guides.summary: Short videos about BeanPool, and the guide pages they go with.

blocks.text: What is in it
In the **Pulse**, tap **Learn**. It holds:

items: videos from BeanPool about how it works;
the **Daily Reflection**, a short thought that changes every morning. It is just a heading; there is nothing to open.

blocks.text: Members can add their own how-to channels to Learn too, by choosing the subject **How it works** when they add a channel. Those videos are the members' own, not BeanPool's: check who posted a video before you follow its advice.
Videos are extra
Everything you need is written in this guide. The videos are there if you would rather watch.
In the Learn lane, tap a video's picture and it plays there in the card. Nothing is loaded from YouTube until you tap. See "The Pulse".
