When BeanPool has made a video for a guide page, and it is in your community's Learn lane, the page shows **Watch:** and the video's name at the top. Tap it to open the video on YouTube. If there is no video for that page, or you are offline, the link simply does not show.
Only BeanPool's own videos ever appear on a guide page. A video a member adds to Learn never shows there, whatever it is called.
Why a video might not show

items: Your phone is offline, or cannot reach your community's server.
A new BeanPool video only appears on guide pages after your community's server is updated.
There is no video for that page yet.

guides.title: Sharing your channels
guides.summary: Put your YouTube, blog, Instagram and other channels on the Pulse.

blocks.text: Add a channel

items: In the **Pulse**, tap **+ Channels**. Or open **Settings** and tap **Channels & Showcase**.
Tap **+ Add a channel**.
Under **Where do you post?**, choose the site.
Type or paste **Your link or handle**.
Under **What's it about?**, choose a subject.
Tap **Add channel**.

blocks.text: Each site works a little differently. The screen says which:

items: **Updates itself** (YouTube, SoundCloud, a blog): new posts appear on the Pulse by themselves.
**A tap per post** (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook): share each post by hand. Where the screen offers **Connect**, you can link the account instead.
**Shows as a card** (a website).

blocks.text: On each channel

items: **Show on the local feed:** switch it off to keep this channel's posts off the Pulse.
**+ Share post:** add one post by hand.
**Make main:** choose your main video channel.
**Remove:** take the channel off.

blocks.text: Sharing one post
Tap **Share a post to Pulse**. Paste the **Post URL**, check which channel and subject it belongs to, and tap **Share to Pulse**.
Remember
Whatever you share to the Pulse is shown with your name and photo. Anyone who opens your community's Pulse can see it, including people who have not joined.

guides.title: Voting on a Decision
guides.summary: Find open Decisions, vote, change your vote, and see results.

blocks.text: Where
Tap **Commons**, then **Decide**. Open Decisions are under **Open Decisions**.

A Decision is binding: if it passes, your community's server carries it out by itself. An admin can stop one only by giving a written reason that members can read. The rules for who can vote, how much turnout is needed and how much Yes is needed are in "Rules and how decisions work".
Reading a Decision
Each Decision shows:

items: what it is about, and what will happen if it passes;
how the votes count: one member one vote, or voice credits for decisions about the Commons' beans;
how long is left. Voting runs for 7 days;
**Turnout:** how many votes it needs, and whether it has them yet;
**Tally:** the Yes and No so far, and how much Yes it needs.

blocks.text: Voting

items: Tap **Vote YES** or **Vote NO**. The app says **Vote Recorded**.
The card then says what you voted, like "You voted Yes".
To change your mind before it closes, tap the other button, such as **Change to No**.

blocks.text: Every Decision is a **secret ballot**. Members see the totals, never who voted how. Your own vote is shown only to you.
Decisions about the Commons' beans

These use **voice credits**. You get voice credits from your completed trades, fresh for each Decision. Use **−** and **+** to choose how many votes to give. More votes cost more: 2 votes cost 4 credits, 3 votes cost 9.
If you have not completed a trade yet, you cannot vote on these. You can still vote on the other Decisions, as long as you joined before they opened and your credit is not frozen.
Results
Tap **Decisions History**. Choose **All**, **Executed**, **Failed** or **Void**. Each shows the final turnout and tally, and what happened, for example that too few people voted.
More
Tap the **ⓘ** next to The Commons for how the Commons' beans and voting work.

guides.title: Proposing a Decision
guides.summary: Ask the community to decide something binding.

blocks.text: Before you start

items: A Decision is for something your community's server can carry out: removing or suspending a member, freezing or unfreezing someone's credit, choosing who may vouch, or paying beans from the Commons. For anything else, start a Poll instead.
You can propose once you have completed a trade, or an admin has given you a trust badge. A vouch alone is not enough.
You can have one open Decision at a time.

blocks.text: Proposing

items: Tap **Commons**, then **Decide**, then **+ Propose a Decision**.
Choose what it is about: **Member** or **Commons Pool**.
**Title:** one line, like "Grant 200 beans to the Tool Library".
**Description & Case:** explain why, in at least 10 characters. Say it plainly. People vote on what they read here.

From the list below that, choose exactly what should happen. For example, for a member: Remove Member, Suspend Member or Freeze Credit. For the Commons: Grant to Enterprise, Hardship Grant or Write Off Deficit.
Fill in who it is for, and how many beans if there are any.
Tap **Submit Community Decision**.

blocks.text: Voting opens at once and runs for 7 days.
If the app says no

items: **Complete a Trade First:** you cannot propose yet.
**Limit Reached:** you already have an open Decision. Wait for it to close.
**Error:** check your description is at least 10 characters long.

guides.title: Polls
guides.summary: Ask the community a quick question. Polls show opinion; they change nothing by themselves.

blocks.text: Poll or Decision?
A **Poll** asks what people think: "Market on Sunday or Saturday?". It changes nothing by itself. For something binding, propose a Decision.
Starting a poll

items: Tap **+ ADD POST** on the Market tab or the Map.
Choose **Community Poll**.
Write the **Question**.
Add **Context / Notes** if it helps. This is optional.
Write 2 to 4 **Options**. Tap **+ Add Option** for more.
Choose how long it runs: **3 Days**, **7 Days** or **14 Days**.
Tap **Create**.

blocks.text: You can have one poll open at a time, and a community can have 5 open at once. You need credit that is not frozen to start or answer a poll.
Finding and answering polls
Polls are in the Market. Tap **Polls** in the top row to see only polls.

items: Tap an answer to choose it. Tap another to change your mind, until the poll closes.
The card shows how many chose each answer.

blocks.text: Polls are not secret. **Your vote is visible to members**: tap **View voters** to see who chose what.
Closing a poll early
If you started it, tap **Close Poll**, then **Close Poll** again to confirm.

guides.title: Events
guides.summary: Create an event, say you are going, be reminded, share it, and run it as the host.

blocks.text: Finding events

items: In the **Market**, tap **Events**. Choose **Today**, **This weekend** or **Next 7 days**.
On the **Map**, tap **Events** to see them as purple pins.

blocks.text: Your events
In the **Market**, tap **★ For You**. **Your events** is the first thing on it: everything you have said you are **Going** to or **Interested** in, soonest first. Tap one to open it.
It is only there when you have something coming up, and it holds only your own answers — nobody else can see it.
Going
On an event, tap **Going** or **Interested**. Tap your choice again to clear it.
When you are **Going**:

items: you can read the host's **Note for people who are going**;
you can open the **event chat**. See "Event chat".

blocks.text: Tap the event to see everything, and **Show on map** to open the place in your phone's maps app.
Being reminded
When you are **Going** or **Interested**, the event shows **Remind me** and how long before it starts you will be told — **1 day before (your default)** until you change it.

items: Tap **Change** to pick **1 week**, **1 day**, **2 hours**, **1 hour** or **30 minutes** before. You can tick more than one.
Tick nothing to get no reminder for this event.
Tap **Use my default** to hand it back to your usual choice.

blocks.text: To change your usual choice for every event, see "Notifications".

Reminders come as alerts on your phone, with your Marketplace alerts, so they stop if you switch those off. You are never reminded about an event that was cancelled or has ended, and never about a time that had already passed when you said you were coming.
Telling someone about it
Open the event and tap **Share**. Your phone's usual share sheet opens with the event's name, when it is, where it is, and a link. On a computer, the link is copied for you to paste.
Anyone who taps that link opens the event — in the app if they have it, in the web app otherwise. Someone who is not in your community lands on its join page.
Putting it in your calendar
Open the event and tap **Add to calendar**.

items: On the **web app**, a calendar file downloads. Open it and your calendar offers to add the event.
On an **iPhone**, the same file is handed to your phone, which offers **Add to Calendar**.
On **Android**, Google Calendar opens with the event already filled in. Check it and save.

blocks.text: The entry carries the name, the time, the place and the link back to the event. If the host later changes the time, your calendar does not change with it — the app will still remind you, and the event itself always shows the new time.
Creating an event

items: Tap **+ ADD POST** on the Market tab or the Map, then **Event**.
**Title**, and when it **Starts**. **Ends** is optional; it is 2 hours later unless you change it.
**Place name**, like "Town hall".
Put the pin on the map: tap the map, search **Find an address**, or tap **Use my location**. Tap **Approximate (~100 m)** if you do not want the exact spot shown. See "Where your pin goes".
A **Description**, and a photo if you like.
**Note for people who are going:** only they will see it. A good place for the exact address or a gate code.
**Who can see it:** your whole community, or one group.

If you keep an enterprise or look after a group, **Post as** lets you post the event in its name. A group hosts for its own members only; an enterprise hosts for the whole community, so an enterprise event is never group-only.
Tap **Create**. Your event is in the Market and on the Map.

blocks.text: Running your event
Open your event. As the host you can:

items: see **Who's going**;
**Edit event**. If you change the time or the place, everyone going is told;
**Copy to a new date**, to run it again;
**Cancel event**, then **Cancel event** again to confirm. Everyone going can see it is cancelled, and its chat becomes read-only.

guides.title: Enterprises and projects
guides.summary: Shared ventures with their own beans: find one, back one, or start one.

blocks.text: What they are

An **enterprise** is something people run together for the community: a tool library, a market stall, a community garden. It has its own beans, its own Offers and Needs, and its own credit line. It is run by **keepers**.

items: A **project** has a goal and usually a deadline, like raising 500 beans for a new roof.
An **ongoing** enterprise keeps going.

blocks.text: Finding them
Tap **Commons**, then **Enterprises**. The **Community Treasuries** come first, then every enterprise with its status, purpose and balance. Tap one to open it.
What an enterprise page shows
Every member can see:

items: its **Purpose**;
its **Balance**, credit line, live Offers and surplus;
**Income & Spend**: every bean in and out;
its keepers;
its **Listings**, **Recent activity** and a **Discussion** you can write in.

blocks.text: At the bottom, **Report Enterprise** if something is wrong.
Backing an enterprise

items: **Pledge beans to a project:** on its page, under the funding box, enter an amount and tap **Pledge Beans**.
**Trade with it:** its Offers and Needs are in the Market like anyone's.
**Become a keeper:** see "Keepers".

blocks.text: Starting one

items: Tap **Commons**, then **Enterprises**, then the round **+** button.
Choose **Bounded Project** or **Ongoing**.
Give it a **Name** and a **Purpose statement**.
For a project, set a **Funding goal** and, if you like, a deadline.
Add a photo if you like.
Tap **Start Initiative**.

blocks.text: It starts straight away, and you are its lead keeper. There is no community vote to start one.
The name, purpose and photo cannot be changed in the app yet.

guides.title: Keepers
guides.summary: The people who run an enterprise and stand behind it. How to join, object, and step down.

blocks.text: What a keeper does
Keepers run an enterprise: they post its Offers and Needs, pay out its beans and look after it. One of them is the **lead keeper**.
A keeper can back the enterprise with some of their own trust. That deepens the enterprise's credit line. It never takes beans from your own balance or your own credit line.
The full rules, including what happens when a lead goes quiet, are in "Rules and how decisions work".
Asking to join

items: Open the enterprise.
Under **Ask to join as a keeper**, enter how much of your trust to back it with. Zero is allowed.
Tap **Request to join as keeper**.

blocks.text: The lead keeper approves or declines. If the enterprise already has more than one keeper, you become a keeper after 3 days, unless another keeper objects.
For keepers

items: **Approve** or **Decline** requests under **Pending keeper requests**.
Changes waiting under **Keeper changes waiting** show the objection window. Tap **Object** to stop one. **Object works on the first tap, with no second question.** One objection cancels the change.
The lead can remove a keeper with **Remove** and their name. Other keepers can object in the same way.
**Operator controls** let keepers post the enterprise's Offers and Needs.

blocks.text: Stepping down
Tap **Step down as keeper**, then **Step down**.

items: The only keeper cannot step down. They can wind the enterprise up instead.
If the enterprise is below zero and needs your backing to cover it, the app says **Not yet**.

blocks.text: When the lead goes quiet
If the lead keeper has not been active for a long time, the other keepers see **Propose Active Keeper as Lead** and can vote **Yes** or **No**. Votes on keepers cannot be changed.

guides.title: The Commons
guides.summary: Your community's shared beans: where they come from, and how they are spent.

blocks.text: What it is
The **Commons** is your community's shared pool of beans. It belongs to everyone.
Beans come into it from:

items: the 1.5% market fee on every completed trade;
the circulation fee on large balances. See "The circulation fee".

blocks.text: Seeing it
Tap **Commons**. At the top, **Commons Pool** shows how many beans it holds. Tap the **ⓘ** next to The Commons for how it works: **How It Works**, **Circulation Fees** and **Voting**.
**Community Treasuries** are listed under **Enterprises**. Tap one to see its balance and every bean in and out. These accounts are open to every member.
Spending it

The Commons' beans are spent only by a community Decision: a grant to an enterprise, a hardship grant to a member, or writing off a debt. See "Proposing a Decision". Decisions about the Commons' beans are counted with voice credits, from completed trades.
The Commons also covers a member's debt when they leave or are removed. See "Leaving or deleting your account".

guides.title: Your balance and history
guides.summary: How many beans you have, what is held, and every trade and gift.

blocks.text: Opening it
Tap **Ledger** in the row of tabs. Your balance is at the top right, in **BEANS**. It can be below zero; see "Your credit line".
The Ledger has two tabs: **Levels** (your trust, see "Trust badges") and **Wallet**. Tap your balance to go straight to Wallet.
The Wallet tab

items: **Your balance**, and roughly how many hours of help it is worth, at 40 beans an hour.
**Commons:** your community's shared pool.
**Credit Floor:** how far below zero you could go.
How many of your beans are held in deals that are under way, when there are some.
**Community Circulation:** shows when you hold beans. See "The circulation fee".
**Project pledges:** beans you have pledged to projects, if any.
**Send Credits:** send a gift. See "Sending a gift".

blocks.text: Recent transactions
Every trade, gift and fee, newest first, with who it was with, a note, the time, and plus or minus. If a note mentions a post, tap **View Offer** to open it.
The list has no search or filters yet.
ⓘ buttons
Tap the **ⓘ** next to Your balance for a short explanation of your balance and your floor.

guides.title: Your credit line
guides.summary: How far below zero you can go, and how it grows.

blocks.text: What it is
Your credit line lets you spend more beans than you have, and go below zero. It is a promise to help others later. Being below zero costs nothing: there is no interest.
Where to see it
On the **Ledger**, under your balance, a bar shows where you are:

items: zero is in the middle;
the left end is **your limit**, the lowest you can go;
the marks on the left show how deep your Offers let you go;
past **+200** on the right is where the circulation fee starts.

blocks.text: Tap the bar for **Credit Slider Info**, which explains each part.
How it opens

It starts at zero. It opens when you complete your first trade in the market (a trade of only 1 or 2 beans is too small to count), or when someone chosen to welcome newcomers vouches for you. Until then the Ledger says **No credit line yet**. You can still trade with beans you hold.
How it grows

items: **Trust:** completed trades build trust, especially with many different people. See "The 500-bean partner limit".
**Ratings:** stars can only lower the trust you earn. An average of 5 stars keeps it all; a lower average takes some off.
The deepest any credit line goes is 2,000 beans.

blocks.text: Your Offers set how much you can use
You can only use as much of your credit line as your live Offers allow:

items: no Offers: none;
1 Offer: down to −200;

blocks.text: The line under the bar tells you, for example "Post an offer to open your credit line".
Spending paused

If you go below what your Offers allow, for example because you took an Offer down, the Ledger says **Spending paused**. You can still earn and sell. Post an Offer, or earn back up, and it lifts. Nothing is taken from you.

guides.title: Sending a gift
guides.summary: Send beans to someone, with no trade.

blocks.text: Before you can

items: You need to have completed a trade in the market. A trade of only 1 or 2 beans is too small to count.
You can only give beans you hold. A gift can never take you below zero.

blocks.text: Until then the button says what is missing, like **needs 1 completed trade** or **needs positive balance**.
Your trust badge does not matter.
Sending

items: Tap **Ledger**, then **Wallet**, then **Send Credits**.
Tap **Select recipient...**, search for their name and tap it.
Type the **Amount**. Add a **Memo** if you like, such as "Thanks for the tomatoes".
Check **Recipient receives**. Gifts have no fee, so they get it all.
Tap **Confirm Transfer**. You see **Sent!**

blocks.text: A gift cannot be taken back. Check the name before you send.
Good to know

items: Gifts do not build trust. Only completed trades do.
You can send gifts while on holiday.

guides.title: Trust badges
guides.summary: Newcomer, Resident, Steward and Elder. What they mean, and why they unlock nothing.

blocks.text: What they are
Your trust badge shows how much trust you have built:

items: **Newcomer:** starting out;
**Resident:** 200 trust;
**Steward:** 600 trust;
**Elder:** 1,400 trust.

blocks.text: A member who has not traded yet shows **FOUNDING** on their posts.
Trust comes from a vouch when you join, from completed trades, and from trust an admin has granted.
They unlock nothing
Badges are recognition, not permission. Every member can post, trade, invite and vote, whatever their badge.
What your trust does change is how deep your credit line can go. See "Your credit line".
Where to see them

items: **Ledger**, then **Levels:** your badge, how much trust you have, and how much more to the next. **All levels** shows every badge; ones you have not reached yet are marked with a lock. That only means "not yet", not that something is locked away.
**What builds your trust:** how much you have traded, with how many people, and your rating.
On posts and profiles, next to each member's name.

blocks.text: In the **Market**, the **Trust** filter can show only posts from members with a certain badge or higher.
Admins and badges
A community's admins can give a member a badge. That deepens their credit line, like earned trust. It does not count as trades: it adds no voice credits and does not let them send gifts.

guides.title: The 500-bean partner limit
guides.summary: Why trading with many people builds more trust than trading a lot with one.

blocks.text: What it limits
When your trust is worked out, trade with any one person counts **up to 500 beans**. Trade beyond that with the same person still happens and still pays. It just adds no more trust.
The same limit applies to your voice credits for votes on the Commons' beans.
What it does not limit
It does not limit how much you can buy, sell, give or receive with anyone. You can trade with one person as much as you both like.
Why

Trust should show that many people found you good to deal with. Two friends swapping beans back and forth should not be able to build a deep credit line on their own. If two people trade a lot and the beans flow almost evenly both ways, their trades with each other count for nothing.
What to do
Trade with more people. Every new trading partner adds to your trust.

guides.title: The circulation fee
guides.summary: A small monthly fee on large balances, so beans keep moving. The first 200 are free.

blocks.text: Why
Beans are for using, not for piling up. A small fee on large balances keeps them moving around the community. It goes to the Commons, for everyone.
How much
Only beans you **hold** above 200 pay. Each part of your balance pays its own rate, per month:

items: the first 200: nothing;

blocks.text: A balance below zero pays nothing. Nobody pays interest on debt.
For example, holding 600 beans for a month costs about 4.5 beans: nothing on the first 200, 3 on the next 300, and 1.5 on the last 100.
When
The fee builds up day by day and is taken a little at a time, whenever your account is next used. You do not lose a lump on one day.
Seeing it

On the **Ledger**, **Wallet**, the **Community Circulation** box shows about how much you will pay this month. It only shows when you hold beans. Above 1,000 beans it turns amber and suggests spending some.
Tap it for **System Circulation**, which explains the fee.
Holiday Mode does not pause the fee.

guides.title: Your privacy
guides.summary: What others can see about you, and the settings that control it.

blocks.text: Opening Settings
Tap the sliders button at the top right of the screen. Settings is not one of the tabs.
What members of your community can see

items: Your name, photo, bio, when you joined and when you were last active.
Your trust badge, how many trades you have done, and your reviews.
Your posts, and where their pins are. See "Where your pin goes".
How you voted on a **Poll**. Votes on **Decisions** are secret.
Your balance and your trades. The app does not show these to others, but a member who knows how can read them from your community's server.

blocks.text: Your posts and their pins, and anything you share to the Pulse, can also be seen by people who have not joined.
What you control

items: **Contact details:** in your profile, choose **Who can see this?**: **Hidden**, **Trade Partners**, **Friends** or **Community**. See "Your profile".

**Location:** in Settings, under **App Settings**, turn **Location** on to use your position for the map and nearby posts. To turn it off, change it in your phone's own settings; the app shows you how.
**App Lock:** asks for your phone's passcode or fingerprint each time the app opens.
**Channels:** anything you share to the Pulse is shown with your name, to anyone who opens the Pulse. See "Sharing your channels".

blocks.text: Who else can see things

items: Chats between two people are usually end-to-end encrypted. See "Messages" for the one exception.

Playing a YouTube video in the Pulse tells YouTube you watched it, the same as opening it in the YouTube app would. Nothing is sent to YouTube until you tap ▶, and scrolling past a video sends nothing at all. See "The Pulse".

Your community's server keeps your trades, posts and votes. The owners and admins who run it can see what is stored there, including event chats and group chats. Choose a community whose people you trust.

blocks.text: Read more
In Settings, under **Legal & Privacy**, tap **Privacy Policy**.

guides.title: Blocking someone
guides.summary: Hide someone's posts and messages from you, and undo it later.

blocks.text: Blocking

items: On their profile: tap **Block**, or **Block** and their name lower down.
On one of their posts: tap **Block User**.
From a chat: tap their name at the top to open their profile, then **Block**.

blocks.text: Confirm with **Block User**.
What it does

items: Their posts in the Market are hidden from you.
They disappear from your People list and your chats, and you cannot message each other.
Their pins on the Map, their Pulse posts, and their messages in event chats still show.
A report goes to your community's moderators, who can look into it.

blocks.text: What it does not do

items: They are not told.
They can still see your posts.
The block is kept on this phone. If you reinstall the app or use another device, block them again.

blocks.text: Unblocking

items: Open **Settings**. Under **Legal & Privacy**, tap **Manage Blocked Users**.
Tap **Unblock** next to a name, or **Unblock All**.

guides.title: Reporting a problem
guides.summary: Tell your community's moderators about a post, an event, a Pulse post or an enterprise.

blocks.text: What you can report

items: **A post in the Market:** open it and tap **Report Post**.
**An event:** open it and tap **Report event**.
**A Pulse post:** tap the flag on it.
**An enterprise:** open it and tap **Report Enterprise** at the bottom.

blocks.text: Then:

items: **A Market post:** choose a reason (**Spam or scam**, **Offensive content**, **Misleading post** or **Other**), add a few words if they help, and tap **Submit Report**.
**A Pulse post:** choose a reason and tap **Submit report**.
**An event:** tap **Report** to confirm.
**An enterprise:** type why, and tap **Submit Report**.

blocks.text: A person or a message
There is no separate button to report a person or a single message in the phone app yet. Block them instead: blocking also sends a report to your community's moderators. See "Blocking someone".
In the web app, a chat with one person has a report button at the top: a flag, with the word **Report** on a wide screen.
What happens next

Your report goes to your community's moderators: the owners and admins who run its server, and any members they have made moderators. They decide what to do. A moderator can remove a post or a Pulse post. Only the owners and admins can suspend a member, while the community votes on it.

items: **A Market post or an event:** if they remove it, you get an alert: "The post you reported was removed". If they look at it and keep it, you are told that too. If its author took it down before they looked, you are told it is no longer up.
**A Pulse post, an enterprise or a person:** you are not told the outcome in the app.
Nobody is told who reported. Not the person you reported, and not anyone else who reported the same thing.

blocks.text: These alerts come under **Marketplace Activity** in your notification settings. See "Notifications".
If one of your own posts is removed by the moderators, you get an alert saying so, and why if they gave a reason. It does not say who reported it.
Now and then the admins clear out old listings to keep the Market tidy. If some of yours are cleared, you get one alert saying how many. That is routine tidying, not a report.
On global.beanpool.org
The global community at global.beanpool.org is open to anyone who signs in, so it looks after itself a little more:

items: **A post reported by three members** who have been there at least a week is hidden at once, until a moderator looks at it. Its author can still see it, and gets an alert that it is hidden, not removed. If the moderators keep it, everyone can see it again.

**New accounts have daily limits** for their first 3 days, and until 3 of their posts have stayed up: 3 posts, 5 photos, and 10 new people to message in any 24 hours. Replying to someone who wrote to you first is never limited. If you reach a limit, the app says which one and when it lets up.
**If the moderators remove three of your posts within 30 days,** you can't post or send messages there until a moderator lifts it. You can still read, edit your profile and leave.

blocks.text: None of this happens in your own local community: there, every report waits for the moderators.
If someone is in danger, contact your local emergency services first.

guides.title: Notifications
guides.summary: Choose which alerts reach your phone, and when events remind you.

blocks.text: Choosing your alerts

items: Open **Settings**. Under **App Settings**, tap **Notification Preferences**.
Switch each kind on or off:
**Direct Messages:** when someone messages you.
**Marketplace Activity:** requests, approvals and refusals on your deals, and what happened to a post you reported or one of yours the admins removed.
**Held in Trust & System:** beans held, released or in question.

blocks.text: Changes save by themselves. They are kept by your community's server, so they follow your account.
Alerts about someone trying to recover your account always come through. You cannot turn those off.
Event reminders

Under the switches, **Event reminders** sets how long before an event you are **Going** to or **Interested** in starts you are told. Tick **1 week**, **1 day**, **2 hours**, **1 hour** or **30 minutes** before — you can tick more than one — or tick **Off** for none at all.
Everyone starts on **1 day** before. This is your usual choice; any one event can be set differently on the event itself. See "Events".

Reminders arrive with your **Marketplace Activity** alerts, so they stop if you switch those off. You are never reminded about an event that was cancelled or has ended, or about a time that had already passed when you said you were coming. If the host moves the event, the reminder moves with it.
No alerts at all?
Check that your phone allows notifications for BeanPool, in your phone's own settings.
One chat at a time
You can mute one group's or enterprise's chat for 8 hours, a week or for good. See "Muting a chat".

guides.title: Light and dark
guides.summary: The app starts light. Make it dark, or follow your phone.

blocks.text: Choosing

items: Open **Settings**. Under **App Settings**, find **Appearance**.
Choose one:
**Same as phone:** the app is dark when your phone is set to dark, and light when it is light.
**Light:** always light. This is how the app starts.
**Dark:** always dark.

blocks.text: When the app is light, **Light Color Scheme** lets you choose **Classic**, **Earth** or **Slate**.
The map has its own light and dark button, on the left of the map.
In the web app, the first choice is called **Same as device**.

guides.title: Going away
guides.summary: Holiday Mode hides your Offers and pauses new requests while you are away.

blocks.text: Turning it on

items: Finish or cancel any deals that are under way first. The app will not start Holiday Mode while you have one.
Open **Settings**. Under **App Settings**, switch on **Holiday Mode**.

blocks.text: While you are away

items: Your posts are hidden from the Market: Offers, Needs, events and polls.
Nobody can send you new requests.
You cannot post or start a deal yourself.
Your balance and your credit line stay as they are.
Gifts still work, and the circulation fee on large balances still applies.

blocks.text: Coming back
Switch **Holiday Mode** off. Your Offers are live again.

guides.title: Leaving or deleting your account
guides.summary: Sign out of this phone, or delete your account for good, and what happens to your beans.

blocks.text: Two choices
Open **Settings** and tap **Account Deletion & Sign Out**, at the bottom. You can:

items: **Remove from This Device Only:** sign this phone out. Your account stays in your community. You can come back with your 12 words, or with a linked sign-in account.
**Permanently Delete Account:** delete your account in this community for good.

blocks.text: Going away for a while? Holiday Mode may be what you want. See "Going away".
Signing out of this phone

items: Tap **Sign Out (Device Only)**.
Type **WIPE** and tap **Confirm Sign Out**.
Pass your phone's lock screen check, then tap **Sign Out** to confirm.

blocks.text: Your account and every community you saved are removed from this phone. A few settings stay, such as your block list. **Without your 12 words you cannot get back in.** Check you have them first.

A phone restored with a sign-in account may have no 12 words. Settings says so. There, **without a linked sign-in account you cannot get back in.** The app says so before you sign out, and **Check Account Protection first** takes you there. If you have the words written down, add them to the phone first (see "Your 12 words").
Deleting your account

items: Tap **Permanently Delete Account**.
Type **DELETE** or your name and tap **Permanently Purge Account**.
Pass your phone's lock screen check, then tap **Permanently Purge** to confirm.

blocks.text: This cannot be undone, even with your 12 words.

items: You cannot delete while you have a deal under way. Finish or cancel it first.
If you hold beans, they go to the Commons.
If you are below zero, the Commons covers the debt.
Your profile becomes "Deleted Member", and your posts come down.
It deletes your account only in the community you are using. Your accounts in other communities stay.

blocks.text: If you run your community's server and you are its only owner, you cannot delete your account until there is another owner.

guides.title: Getting your account back
guides.summary: Restore your account on a new phone, and protect it with a sign-in account.

blocks.text: On a new phone

items: Install BeanPool and open it.
Tap **Already a Member? Restore Account**.
Choose **Recover with 12 Words** or **Recover with Social**.

blocks.text: With your 12 words

items: Type the 12 words in order, or tap **Paste**.
Type your community's name or address.
Tap **Recover Identity**. Your name and photo come back from your community.

blocks.text: With a sign-in account
This works only if you linked one before (see below), and only while your community's server is running.

items: Type your name in the community. The app may suggest "Is this you?".
Type your community's name or address.
Tap **Recover with** and the account you linked: Google, Facebook or GitHub, or Apple on an iPhone.

With Google on an iPhone, a Google web page opens. Sign in there and choose the account you linked. On Android, Google shows its own list of accounts. If it can't show one on that phone, a Google web page opens instead.

With GitHub, the app shows a code, already copied, and what to do on GitHub. Tap **Open GitHub** (on an iPhone, GitHub's page opens by itself). On GitHub, press and hold the first box and choose **Paste**, then approve. When GitHub says you're all set, tap **✕** at the top left to come back (an iPhone comes back by itself). Tap **Copy** to copy the code again, or **Open GitHub** to get back to the page. While the app is waiting for GitHub, **Cancel** stops it. When GitHub confirms, the code and **Cancel** go away and the app finishes getting your account back.

blocks.text: If the sign-in account was linked from a phone that had your 12 words, on an up-to-date app, your 12 words come back too. Otherwise the phone has no 12 words: they can't be rebuilt from a sign-in. If you have them written down, you can add them (see "Your 12 words"). Until then a linked sign-in account is that phone's way back, so keep one linked, and link a second one if you can (see below).
Protecting your account now

items: Open **Settings** and tap **Account Protection**.
Under **Sign-In Recovery Providers**, tap **Protect with** and choose an account.
With Google on an iPhone, a Google web page opens. Sign in there and choose your account, and you come back to BeanPool.

With GitHub, the app shows a code and copies it. Tap **Open GitHub**, press and hold the first box and choose **Paste**, then approve. When GitHub says you're all set, tap **✕** at the top left to come back to BeanPool (an iPhone comes back by itself). The app links your account as soon as you are back. While the app is waiting for GitHub, **Cancel** stops it.

blocks.text: This works on a phone with no 12 words too.

If this phone has your 12 words, the linked account keeps them as well, so restoring with it gives them back. An account you linked on an older version of the app keeps only your key: tap **Connect again** next to it to include the words. On a phone with no 12 words there is nothing to include, so **Connect again** is not shown.
GitHub works only once your community's server has been updated for it. Until then the app says so. Use Google, Apple or your 12 words instead.
This is not a way to log in. Your account is still your own key. The linked account only helps you get it back, in that community.
To remove it, tap **Disconnect**.
If someone else tries

If someone starts recovering your account, you get an alert, and Settings shows **Someone is recovering your account**. If it is not you, tap **Stop It Now**. If they used your linked sign-in account, they may already be in by the time you see it. Keep that sign-in account safe, with its own strong password.
If the phone already has an account

Restoring a different account replaces the one on this phone. The app asks you to type **WIPE** first. Make sure you have the 12 words for the account you are replacing. If this phone has no 12 words for that account (Settings says so), without a linked sign-in account you cannot get it back.
Lost everything?
Without your 12 words and without a linked sign-in account, only the admins of your community can help, by setting you up again.

guides.title: Your 12 words and the server's keys (owners)
guides.summary: For a community's owners. Checking your 12 words, taking over or restoring the server with your phone, and the check your phone makes by itself.

blocks.text: Who this is for
Only a community's **owners**. If you are not an owner, you won't see any of this.
Why owners are asked

Your community's server keeps a locked copy of its keys, for moving the community to another server if its own is lost, and its backups are locked too. They are locked to the owners' accounts: any one owner can open them with their phone (see Taking over or restoring with your phone, below). If you lose your phone, your 12 words bring your account back, and with it your key to the server's lock and its backups. That matters most on the day the server itself is gone.
So the app asks each owner, now and then, to check they still have the right 12 words. You can say **Later**. Nothing is ever blocked, and you can keep doing everything an owner does.
When the app asks

items: Once, soon after you become an owner.
Again 12 months after your last check.

blocks.text: It shows a card at the top of the Market (in the web app, at the top of every screen but the Map): **Check now** or **Later**. **Later** puts the card away until the next time it is due. You can check any time from **Settings**: under **Community keys**, tap **Check your 12 words** (in the web app, **Check now**).
How to check

items: Get your paper with the 12 words.
Type them in order, with spaces between them. Capitals and extra spaces don't matter.
Tap **Check my words**.

blocks.text: If they are right, the app says **These are the right words**. If not: **These aren't the words for this account.** It doesn't say which word is wrong, so check the paper and type them all again.

On a phone with no copy of your 12 words (one restored with a sign-in account), right words also bring **Save them on this phone**. Tap it and **View Recovery Phrase** shows them from then on. It is the same check and the same save as **Add your 12 words to this phone** (see "Your 12 words").

Can't find them? If this phone still has them, **Settings**, then **View Recovery Phrase**, shows them. Write them down again, then check. On a phone with no copy, the app says so: when you find them, check them here, then save them.
What is sent, and what is not

items: The check happens on your phone (or in your browser, in the web app). Your words are never sent anywhere. The box is emptied as soon as the check answers, and when you leave the screen. They are saved only if you tap **Save them on this phone**, and then only on this phone.
When the words are right, your phone tells your community's server only that you checked, and when, signed with your account.
Owners and admins see, in the server's Settings, each owner's "12 words checked" date, or "not yet". It is your own statement: the server cannot see or check your words.

blocks.text: Taking over or restoring with your phone

If your community's server is lost, whoever runs its standby server (or a new server restoring a backup) can ask an owner to open the locked keys. Any one owner is enough. You need the newest version of the BeanPool app. The web app works too if it still opens, but it lives at your community's own address, which may be down with the server: the phone app is the one to count on.

items: On the server's Settings, they choose **Take over with an owner's phone**, or **Open with an owner's phone** when restoring a backup. A code appears on their screen.

In the app: **Settings**, under **Community keys**, tap **Take over or restore with this phone**, and point the camera at the code. If the server's page is open on your own phone, tapping its link does the same. In the web app, copy the link from their screen and paste it under **Take over or restore with this browser** in **Settings**.
The app shows which community, which server, and what will happen. If your main server still answers, it says so in red: a take-over is only for a server that is really gone.

Tap **Unlock for the take-over** (or **Unlock the backup**). Your phone asks for its own unlock first: fingerprint, face or PIN. The web app has no such step, which is why the phone app is the safer place for an owner's key.
Your phone opens its own part of the lock and hands the key to that server, locked so only that server can read it. Your phone never sees the server's keys or the backup.
On a take-over, the person at the server then confirms on their screen. The community is told it moved, and that you opened the keys.

blocks.text: The app refuses, and says why, if the lock belongs to another community, if it is not locked to you, if the server's code has run out (it lasts 10 minutes and works once), or if the keys were not locked by your community's own server.
Your phone checks the lock by itself

Each time your community's lock changes (an owner is added or removed, a new recovery code is made), your app checks, quietly, that it could still open its part. It opens it, throws the key away at once, and tells the server whether it worked. Nothing is asked of you.

Owners and admins see it in the server's Settings, next to your 12 words date: **their phone opened the current lock**, with the date, or that it last opened an older one. If it says your phone **could NOT open** the lock, check your 12 words, and ask another owner to look at the server's Settings.
